key_claims: Fed released minutes of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting on Nov 18 (US time); 'almost all' participants judged further increases in the target range 'could be appropriate'; 'many' see the AI investment boom as a significant inflation-risk source (attributed to Yahoo Finance).
October meeting held rates at 3.75%-4.00%; Hammack and Cook dissented in favor of a hike.

Governor Waller, before the minutes release, argued the December meeting may need a 50bp hike; core CPI running 0.3% m/m for three months; 'Fed needs to break the psychology that 3% inflation is normal' (attributed to CoinDesk). US 2y yield +4.1bp to 4.83% early that day.
CME FedWatch: >95% priced for a 25bp hike at the Dec 9 meeting (attributed to CryptoTicker); up from ~85% the prior week.
Wednesday Nov 18: Dow -1.15% (first time since Oct 2008 with three straight sessions down >1%); S&P 500 -0.3%; Nasdaq +0.35% (attributed to CoinDesk). Gold -2.35% to $3,774/oz, 14-month low.
Gold stabilizing near $3,730/oz after Wednesday's -3.2% drop (lowest close since Sep 2025); minutes show almost all officials see further hikes needed in coming months to return inflation to 2%.
Waller said Wednesday inflation is moving in the wrong direction and urged considering a 50bp hike in December.
Market pricing three 25bp hikes by June next year; a dollar index gauge rose 0.4% Wednesday.
Gold also caught in AI-equity selling as the post-NVDA-earnings rally faded; Wall Street volatile again.

FOMC minutes: almost all Fed officials in October judged further hikes may be needed in coming months; 'a few' policymakers said a December hike may need to be 'more than 25bp' if inflation data disappoint.
Waller: Fed needs to be more aggressive on hikes; should hike 50bp in December if not signaling a January hike.
PBoC publishes November LPR on Nov 20 at 09:15 (Beijing time).
NY Fed-side commodity wrap: WTI -3.65% to $82.87; COMEX gold -3.53% to $3,727.80.

Minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting: 'almost all' members saw further action at the next meeting as appropriate; two officials argued for defending a hike of 25bp or MORE at the December FOMC; Hammack and Cook supported hiking.
Waller (CNBC interview on the 18th): inflation moving in the wrong direction, broadening; Fed should consider 50bp in December; his threshold for a large hike was core inflation 0.3% m/m.
October CPI came in above expectations, strengthening the case for a 50bp discussion.
Several officials supported holding but called the decision 'finely balanced'; staff warned of significant risk of disorderly rise in 5-year inflation expectations.
Overall hawkish; short-term markets fully price a December hike; focus shifts to hike size; dollar likely to stay firm.
NOTE: this article's opening sentence contains an internally inconsistent date ('Oct 27 published minutes of Oct 28 meeting') — treated as a translation typo; release date Nov 18 per CFTime/Jin10.

NY Nov 18 close: Dow 50,198.17 (-561.25); Nasdaq 24,429.89 (+101.51). NVDA earnings well received, easing AI worries and lifting tech; UNH/healthcare dragged the Dow; hawkish minutes + Waller 50bp remarks kept the Dow under pressure all day.
FX Nov 18 NY close: USDJPY 159.35 (range 159.13-159.48); EURUSD 1.0973; GBPUSD 1.3147; EURJPY 174.85.
Eurozone October final CPI +4.0% y/y, as expected (London session data).
UK inflation easing cooled BoE hike expectations; sterling sold off. BoE Bailey: growth improving; longer Middle East conflict lasts, the more rates need to stay high.
US Oct housing starts 1.309M (consensus 1.25M); building permits 1.295M (consensus 1.375M); pending home sales -4.7% m/m (consensus -2.0%).
SF Fed Daly: labor market stable but little growth momentum; inflation too high for a long time; policy supports a cautious approach.

FOMC minutes quotes: 'almost all' see further action appropriate; two policymakers argued for >25bp in December; many see AI diffusion as an important upside inflation risk; most see inflation pressures broadening.
